Growth behaviour

Network coarseness6.5.0

One control over sensor spread, reach, step and trail bias — low gives a fine dense mesh, high gives long arterial routes with large enclosed voids.

Deposit strength0.50
Evaporation0.9350
Diffusion0.30

Diffusion spreads the trail sideways each step. The original had none, which is why its networks read as scratchy; a little makes them cohere into veins.

Advanced kinematics
Sensor angleauto
Sensor distanceauto
Turn rateauto
Step lengthauto

Zero means follow the coarseness control. Move a slider to override it.

Agents per seed6000

Terrain response

Terrain influence1.00

Master multiplier on every weight below. At zero the mould ignores the map entirely and you get pure Physarum.

Per-surface weights
Negative repels, positive attracts. The defaults follow the project’s own rules: National Landscape, water and flood zone 3 are effectively hard exclusions, while the proposed orbital, the rail network and the towns marked to join the belt pull growth towards them.

The stations

Clearance, primary6.0 km
Clearance, secondary4.2 km
Clearance, additional3.0 km
Push strength4.0

Each station pushes the mould off its own ground, so a cell closes around it and the railway crosses the interior — the drawing already developed downstream. Attraction was tried first and does nothing: the sensor reaches about 2.7 km, so a bump 3 km wide is only felt once an agent has arrived. Radius is the mechanism; strength is a threshold, and past about 2 nothing further changes.

Station trail0.00

Trail laid at each station every step — Tero’s oat flake. Unlike the clearance dent this one diffuses, so its gradient carries past the sensor. Off by default: the station cells come from the dent, not from this.

The corridor

Free width6 km

Half-width either side of the spine where the ground carries no penalty at all. Keep this well under the belt's natural reach or the fade below has nothing to act on: at 10 km, nine tenths of the mould sits inside this zone and never feels the ramp at all.

Fade over20 km
Fade strength6.0

Beyond the free width the ground turns against the mould, so growth thins out rather than stopping at a line. At zero the corridor is off and the mould has the whole sheet.

Edge shape2.0

How the fade bites. 1.0 is even, 2.0 is slow to start then sharp, 3.0 reaches further out then cuts harder.

The cells round the stations

Vein threshold0.20
Grow into the veins1.5 km
The run pauses at step 900, the state the booklet measures. Then find the cells: the ground the veins close off all round, grown out to the middle of the vein round it, so neighbouring cells share one edge. Open ground (outside the loop, inside it, or cut off by the sheet's edge) is not a cell.

Both in British National Grid metres (EPSG:27700). The baked set for the wool chat, from the Python twin of this model at seed 42, is in 03_Station cells for the wool chat.
